text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The leading government party the Coalition Party and the opposition party the Centre Party signed a cooperation agreement and elected new city leaders for Tallinn. Newspapers predict a government crisis.
- Police chief Ain Seppik denies that Imre Perli, the compiler of the pirate data base which contained confidential information on people, was hired for this task by the police.
- Estonians and Russians are the main foreign offenders in Finland, Finnish Interior Minister Jan-Erik Enestam said although official statistics prove differently.
- Recent explanations by Foreign Minister Siim Kallas only increased the confusion surrounding the technical border agreement with Russia, parliament vice-president Tunne Kelam said.
- Media officials discussed merging public TV and radio to form the Estonian Broadcasting Company.
- Police sources said several Estonian newspapers had used the pirate data which was sold on the black market.
- The number of legal owners of firearms in Tallinn is growing constantly by 30 people a month and is now at 11,723.
- Talks over a pay deal at the huge Kreenholm textile plant were successful and a strike was averted.
- Parliament discussed a draft law on pensions and plans to raise the monthly amount by 65 kroons.
- If agreement between Estonian and Scandinavian aviation officials is not found flights between the Baltic state, Denmark and Sweden may be suspended from today.
